clue.text: Bets involving first three rugby scores without backing record

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the scores sit around the other piece

parts.note: a try is the main score in rugby, so several of them are tries

indicators.note: backing means the record's letters go in backwards, as a car reverses

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A punter backs rugby scorers early in the game while failing to set a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns LP into PL, and 'without' (meaning outside) wraps TRIES around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A triple is a wager picking the first three finishers, so bets of that kind fit the plural.

clue.text: Little one's heart becoming dead large

indicators.note: the heart of 'one' is its middle letter N, which turns into another letter

parts.note: a little one is tiny; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A small child's heart grows hugely after death, a strange piece of anatomy.
explanation.walkthrough: The N swapped out is the central letter of 'one', and in TINY that N is replaced by D.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidy is informal for considerable in size, as in a tidy sum of money.

clue.text: Concerning, having flipped a bit?

indicators.note: flipped means the letters picked out of that word are then read in reverse
a bit of the word Concerning is taken, a run of its inner letters

explanation.surface: A question about something to do with a minor reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit' takes ERNI from the middle of 'Concerning'; 'having flipped' turns it round. The definition is the same word the letters come from, so the whole clue does both jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means with regard to, a formal synonym of about or regarding.

clue.text: Most strong flush wiping edges to toilet — sit oddly

indicators.note: wiping the edges off the word flush leaves only its inner letters
oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of each of the two following words

explanation.surface: Lavatory instructions: a vigorous flush, wipe round the rim, and sit at a funny angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes TIE from 'toilet' and ST from 'sit', added after LUS from 'flush'; 'to' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusty means vigorous and robust, so its superlative is the most powerful or hearty.

clue.text: Smooth razor — bend for end of tash

indicators.note: one letter for another means a swap, the bend replacing a letter

parts.note: to razor is to shave

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of tash

parts.note: a U-bend is the curved pipe under a sink, so a bend gives U

explanation.surface: A barber chats about a smooth razor and curving it to finish off a moustache.
explanation.walkthrough: The H at the end of 'tash' (slang for moustache) is the letter replaced, giving S-U-AVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Suave describes a polished, urbane manner, the figurative sense of smooth.

clue.text: Rule around edge of pavement, mostly for pedestrian

indicators.note: around signals the rule's letters turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a law is a rule

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: the kerb is the edge of a pavement (British spelling of curb)

explanation.surface: A highway-code style rule about keeping walkers back from the kerb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns LAW into WAL, and 'mostly' trims KERB to KER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestrian is someone travelling on foot, which is exactly what a walker does.

clue.text: Once more question/answer dropped from toothpaste

indicators.note: dropped from says the letters for question and answer are removed from the brand name

parts.note: Aquafresh is a well-known brand of toothpaste

explanation.surface: Like a quiz show losing its question-and-answer round from a toothpaste advert.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing QU and then A from AQUAFRESH leaves A + FRESH.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something afresh is to do it again, starting anew.

clue.text: Tease, recalling the Guardian 1 down — primarily it's used to write "little one"

parts.note: to kid is to tease

indicators.note: recalling, calling back, means these pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: the Guardian's writers would call themselves we
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of down

parts.note: ink is what a pen uses to write

explanation.surface: The paper's 1 down clue was Little one, so a cheeky note asks which spelling of the childish word the Guardian uses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalling' turns WE + I + D into DIEW. The clue refers to 1 down, whose clue begins 'Little one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiddiewink is a jokey British word for a small child, a little one.

clue.text: New Nike grass design — they're slippery on grass?

indicators.note: design signals that the letters are reworked into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A new style of Nike trainer for grass courts turns out to be slippery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' rearranges N + NIKE + GRASS. The ring snake is the grass snake, so the definition puns on slippery creatures on a lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring snakes are a name for grass snakes, smooth reptiles found slithering through grassland.

clue.text: Actress to act, lines to go over said in the wrong order

parts.note: to do is to act

indicators.note: the lines go over, covering, the shuffled word

parts.note: RY, short for railway, gives lines

indicators.note: in the wrong order means the word said is rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor going over lines in rehearsal says them all in the wrong order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wrong order' turns SAID into ISDA, which 'to go over' puts inside RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris Day was an American film star and singer of the 1950s and 1960s.

clue.text: Leader of gladiators to fall, captivating 500 amphitheatre seats

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
captivating means holding the other piece prisoner inside

parts.note: to rain is to fall from the sky
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: The head gladiator falls in the arena, thrilling the crowds of spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradin is one of a series of tiered steps or seats, as in an amphitheatre.

clue.text: Oliver, perhaps, or Tom out of Lloyd Webber work?

indicators.note: out of means the name Tom is taken out of the musical's title

parts.note: The Phantom of the Opera is a musical by Andrew Lloyd Webber

explanation.surface: A theatre fan wonders whether Oliver or Tom was dropped from a Lloyd Webber show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oliver' looks like the musical, and it is: Oliver Twist is the parentless boy, while 'Tom' is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist is a famous parentless child, an example of the answer, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Re Special K — inspire mix without nuts: Alpen cereal?

indicators.note: mix signals that the long phrase is rearranged
nuts says the brand name is jumbled too, and without says its letters are taken away from the mix

explanation.surface: Breakfast advertising: Special K inspires a nut-free blend, unlike muesli brand Alpen.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle RESPECIALKINSPIRE, take out the letters of ALPEN, and the twelve left make the answer. Special K and Alpen are breakfast cereal brands.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice Krispies is a long-running Kellogg's breakfast cereal of puffed rice.

clue.text: They're in purse to steal money dropping heroin over road …

parts.note: to swipe is to steal

indicators.note: over means the trimmed money is placed over, around, the road
dropping says the letter for heroin is removed

parts.note: cash is money
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A thief swipes a purse for money, then drops drugs as they flee over the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' takes H from CASH, giving CAS, and 'over' puts it around RD.
explanation.definitionFit: Swipe cards are plastic access or payment cards, the kind kept in a purse.

clue.text: … compromised dealing? Dog intercepting traffic — international cocaine concealed

indicators.note: intercepting means the dog cuts into the other word
concealed means those letters are hidden away, removed from the word

parts.note: taken as written
C is slang for cocaine
a dingo is an Australian wild dog

explanation.surface: A sniffer dog intercepts drug trafficking, with cocaine smuggled across borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed' removes IC from TRAFFIC, leaving TRAFF, which DINGO splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Trading off means balancing one thing against another, a compromise in a deal.

clue.text: The articulated engineering shows dirt crossing motorway

indicators.note: crossing means the shuffled letters lie across, around, the motorway
engineering means the letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Engineering works on a motorway leave dirt everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineering' rearranges SHOWS DIRT into WORDSITHS, and 'crossing' puts it around M after WORDS. 'The articulated' are people who speak well, used as a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsmiths are skilled writers, people who are especially fluent with words.

clue.text: Ariel's ground here

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the name's letters are broken up and remade

parts.note: Ariel's read as Ariel is, keeping the S

explanation.surface: A spirit's homeland, or the land a politician called Ariel stands on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges ARIELS. As a whole, it is the land of Ariel Sharon, or the settlement of Ariel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is both a city in this country and the first name of its former prime minister Sharon.

clue.text: Jock's query with hard answer

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A Scotsman puzzles over a question with a difficult reply.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Scots form of who, a question a Scot (Jock) might ask.

clue.text: Point out initial letters

parts.note: to initial a document is to sign it
post is letters and mail

explanation.surface: Two words on the first letters of words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initial' and 'letters' look like one idea, initial letters, but split into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To signpost something is to indicate it or point it out clearly.

clue.text: School introduction to "pi by diameter" — grasping circumference

indicators.note: grasping means the first letters hold the circle between them
introduction to takes the first letter of each of the two words

parts.note: O is a circle, a circumference

explanation.surface: A maths lesson introducing pi times the diameter to find a circle's circumference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' is the definition, a group of whales, not a classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A pod is a group of whales or dolphins, just as a school is.

clue.text: Quickly passing state as Simon ultimately follows Garfunkel's return — calm line taken

indicators.note: follows puts Simon's last letter after the returned name
return means the first name is read backwards

parts.note: Art Garfunkel, the singing partner of Paul Simon

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of Simon
taken means the line is taken away from the calm word

parts.note: silence is calm

explanation.surface: Simon and Garfunkel reunite in calm after a passing quarrel, a nod to The Sound of Silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' makes TRA, 'follows' adds N after it, and 'taken' drops L from SILENCE to leave SIENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Transience is the condition of being brief or fleeting, existing only for a short while.

clue.text: Playing lead in Casino Royale, actor is great primarily

definitions.text: Playing lead in Casino Royale, actor is great primarily

indicators.note: playing means the two words are moved about into a new order
primarily takes the first letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Praise for the star of the Bond film Casino Royale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' rearranges LEAD IN into DANIEL; 'primarily' takes CRAIG from Casino Royale actor is great.
explanation.definitionFit: He took the lead role of James Bond in the 2006 film Casino Royale.

clue.text: After operation cancels vet — carries on improving health

indicators.note: carries means the shuffled letters hold the other word inside
operation means working on the letters, which are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pet recovering after surgery cancels its vet appointment and carries on getting better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After operation' rearranges CANCELS VET into CVALESCENT, which 'carries' ON after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: A convalescent patient is recovering, getting stronger after illness.

clue.text: See 21
Long for girl …

definitions.meaning: to yearn for something absent, to pine for it
a title for a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A wistful line about yearning for a girl, leading into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Missing someone is longing for them, and the same word is the title of a young woman.

clue.text: … Tramp head over heels with kiss off top girl

indicators.note: head over heels means tumbling, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Tramp is the setter, so the setter's name gives me

indicators.note: off means the kiss is taken off the word for top

parts.note: max is the top, as in to the max
X is the sign of a kiss

explanation.surface: Tramp falls head over heels for a girl and kisses her, a romantic follow-on from the clue before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head over heels' turns ME into EM; MAX with X taken off leaves MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a common girl's name, and the heroine of the Jane Austen novel.

clue.text: Piece that is for beginner

parts.note: a rook is a chess piece
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A chess lesson about a piece suitable for a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a novice or newcomer, someone just starting out.

clue.text: Low Haye cut is back — boxing is thuggery

indicators.note: boxing means the pieces close round the other word as in a box
back means the two pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: cut means the final letter of the name is lopped off

explanation.surface: Boxer David Haye's low blow comes back to haunt him: boxing is just thuggery.
explanation.walkthrough: David Haye is a British boxer. 'back' turns MOO + HAY into YAHOOM, and 'boxing' puts IS inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Yahooism is crude, boorish behaviour, after the brutish Yahoos of Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: Round feet will ultimately crack casing of Steinway piano

indicators.note: crack means the pieces break into the gap between those outer letters
casing of takes the outer letters of Steinway

parts.note: O is round

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of will

explanation.surface: A round foot will eventually crack the case of a Steinway grand piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piano' is the musical direction meaning quietly, not the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano in music means to play quietly, gently, without force.

clue.text: Set sail before a bird embraces pussycat's tail

indicators.note: before places the bird piece ahead of the a
embraces means the bird holds the other letter inside

parts.note: a goose is a bird

indicators.note: tail takes the last letter of pussycat's

explanation.surface: A nod to the Owl and the Pussycat, who went to sea in a pea-green boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The owl and the pussycat of Edward Lear's poem went to sea; here the bird is a goose.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to sea is to set out on a voyage, setting sail.
